title: api-config runtime architecture sketch
content:
Personal scratchpad for api-config -> runtime integration. Informal notes, questions, sketches. DO NOT USE AS FINAL SPEC.

Context / problem summary:
- We need a compact API-level config shape that can express runtime hints for serving: preferred kernel/quantization profile, batching policy, kv-cache controls, and fallback routing preferences.
- Goal: simple default-able shape for hosted API while allowing Dedicated/Private overrides.
- Must be easy to store as customer config, pin to model-version, and reference in rollout metadata.

High-level requirements (non exhaustive):
- readable by control plane and runtime router
- can express per-endpoint overrides (chat vs embed vs rerank)
- backward compatible: new fields are optional, unknown fields ignored
- small surface so product can explain to customers

Initial sketch of API config shape (not strict JSON schema, just first pass):

api_config: {
  version: "v1",                       # bump when we add breaking fields
  model_pin: "redwood/gpt-4x-1.0",    # optional model reference
  profile: "balanced" | "latency" | "throughput" | "cost",
  quantization: {
    preferred: "int8" | "int4" | "fp16" | "auto",
    allowed_fallbacks: ["int8","fp16"]
  },
  batching: {
    max_tokens_per_batch: 2048,         # hard cap per GPU batch
    target_latency_ms: 200,             # soft SLO for autoscaler hints
    prefer_dyn_batch: true              # allow dynamic batching optimizations
  },
  cache: {
    enabled: true,                      # prefix / KV cache enabled for this endpoint
    ttl_seconds: 3600,                  # eviction hint for control plane
    storage_tier: "in_memory" | "remote"
  },
  routing: {
    priority: "latency" | "cost" | "regional",
    fallback_models: ["redwood/gpt-4x-0.9-quant"],
  },
  observability: {
    sample_rate: 0.01,                   # token-level sampling for traces/metrics
    send_payloads: "never" | "errors_only" | "all"
  }
}

Notes on shape choices and open questions:
- "profile" is a product-friendly knob. Internally maps to sets of recommended batching/quantization/routing choices. Keep mapping in control plane.
- quantization.preferred vs allowed_fallbacks: runtime should try preferred first and fallback if incompatible with hardware or performance. That implies we need runtime API to report back which variant is used (for billing/telemetry).
- cache.storage_tier: in_memory vs remote. For Dedicated with multi-GPU, we may want per-GPU in-memory + remote backing for cold starts. How do we express multi-level caching? Maybe add "cache.layers" later. For now keep one tier.
- batching.target_latency_ms: ambiguous semantics. Is it per-request SLO or hint for autoscaler? We'll store as a hint and make runtime decide. Add explicit field later to separate SLO vs hint.

Runtime sketch (how control plane -> runtime consumes it):
1) Customer saves api_config with endpoint creation. Control plane validates shape (schema v1).
2) On deploy/pin, control plane compiles a runtime manifest: merges defaults + profile mapping + endpoint overrides -> a flattened runtime_manifest JSON. This manifest is what the runtime agent reads.
3) Runtime agent exposes health/telemetry reporting including: effective_quantization, batch_sizes, cache_hit_rate, chosen_fallback_model, and a manifest_version.
4) Rollouts reference manifest_version to ensure deterministic rollbacks.

Minimal example of runtime_manifest (flattened):
- manifest_version: "20250302-9b3f"
- effective_quantization: "int8"
- batch_target_ms: 200
- kv_cache_enabled: true
- fallback_used: null or "redwood/gpt-4x-0.9-quant"

ASCII diagram (very rough):

  [control plane] --(compile manifest)-> [runtime router / agent] --(requests)--> [GPU pool nodes]
                                              |                                      |
                                              |-- telemetry --> telemetry pipeline       |-- model artifacts (weights)

Notes on runtime behaviour we need to implement: 
- manifest should be small and cacheable by the runtime agent. Use an etag / version id.
- need a lightweight polling path for private deployments; hosted can push. Private may poll every n seconds and accept long-poll change notifications.
- when runtime chooses a fallback model variant, it must annotate request traces so control plane can surface to user. (TODO: schema for trace annotation)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How many profiles should we ship initially? Minimal: balanced, latency, cost. Possibly throughput for batch-only workloads.
- Q: How to express GPU affinity? e.g., prefer A100 vs H100 or prefer fp16-capable nodes. Right now we rely on routing policies independent from api_config; might add node_affinity field later.
- Q: Billing implications for quantization fallback. If preferred int4 not available and int8 used, unit cost changes. Need fields in manifest for "billing_variant". Add to runtime_manifest.
- TODO: align with product on examples page (console) showing common template configs for chat vs embeddings. (Jamie to own)
- TODO: add a compact JSON Schema + example validators in rfc repo (see linked GH PR).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep v1 conservative: optional fields only, clear defaults.
- Focus on runtime telemetries that enable diagnosability: chosen_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate.
- For Dedicated/Private, add "override_layers": [control_plane, infra_admin] where infra_admin can pin quantization for compliance.

Quick guesstimate UX mapping:
- console: profile dropdown + toggle for "enable cache" + advanced JSON editor (collapses unknown fields)
- API: create endpoint accepts api_config payload. Later support PATCH to update live manifest with canary rollout semantics.

Links / references:
- RFC draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/87
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ENG/API+Config+RFC
- Jira: ENG-1245 (api-config runtime integration)

End of scratchpad.

Last edits: quick sync with Casey on 2025-03-02 (notes appended inline re: polling interval).

Polling decision: for private deployments default poll interval = 60s, allow override to 15s for low-latency infra. Note: we need to rate-limit poll bursts.

Unresolved: final naming for "quantization.preferred" vs "preferred_variant". Might rename to preferred_variant to encompass e.g. "gpt4x-int8-kernel-v2" later.
